clue.text: Type of blood supplement that is criminal

blocks.note: B is one of the four blood groups
to supplement is to add to
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'; with the following 'is' it reads 'that is'

explanation.surface: A blood-boosting supplement that turns out to be illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'that is' gives IE (id est); the clue's 'is' does double duty as the end of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A baddie is an informal word for a villain or wrongdoer, so a criminal person.

clue.text: Tying up promise ahead of time  …

blocks.note: a bond is a binding promise
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Making a commitment in advance that ties you down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is the state of being bound or tied, so tying up describes it as a noun phrase.

clue.text: …  start to remove objection, perhaps

blocks.note: de- is the prefix meaning to remove, as in de-ice
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 down: a first step towards getting rid of a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DE-BUT, the answer literally means removing a 'but', which is an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance or performance, the start of a career.

clue.text: E-learning is customised mostly

indicators.note: customised means altered to suit, so the letters before it are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Online learning courses are largely tailored to the individual.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or for the most part, a straightforward synonym for mostly.

clue.text: Queen taking in strip show

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a queen is a female cat
to strip is to bare

explanation.surface: A monarch attending a striptease performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like ER or R, but here it is a female cat; 'strip show' wants to be read together, but only 'show' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is entertainment with music and dancing at a nightclub, so a kind of show.

clue.text: Arrests that often require cuffs, or ties

definitions.text: that often require cuffs, or ties

blocks.note: first meaning: to collar someone is informally to arrest them

blocks.clueFragment: that often require cuffs, or ties
blocks.note: second meaning: parts of shirts, which go with cuffs and are worn with ties

explanation.surface: Police detentions that usually need handcuffs or restraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuffs' suggests handcuffs for arrests, but it also points to shirt cuffs, which go with shirt necks worn with ties.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the neckbands of shirts, while the verb is police slang for seizing suspects.

clue.text: Second connection in very short time

blocks.note: B is the second letter or second grade
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: Getting a follow-up connection made almost instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A blink of an eye is an idiom for an instant, a tiny moment.

clue.text: It's really dangerous helping to hold up support

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a ration is a helping or portion
aid is support

explanation.surface: A warning that lending a hand to prop something up is very risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiation can cause serious harm to living tissue, so it is described as something hazardous.

clue.text: Goethe Medal has focused on single subject  …

indicators.note: has means contains, so the letters sit inside the words before it

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A literary award named after Goethe concentrates on one topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something themed is organised around one particular topic or motif.

clue.text: …  said to be somewhat overbalanced

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so only some of the next word is used

blocks.note: found inside the word

explanation.surface: Continuing from 7 down: a claim that something is a little lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal means spoken rather than written, as in a verbal agreement.

clue.text: Load being dispersed is nothing special

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spreading a heavy load around is not a big issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is both part of the letters to rearrange and part of the signal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: No big deal is an idiom for something unimportant or ordinary.

clue.text: Popular cross over musical style  …

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
to cross over is a euphemism for dying

explanation.surface: A well-liked crossover genre of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross over' suggests crossover music, but it means passing to the other side, that is, dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a genre of rock and pop originally from independent record labels.

clue.text: …  playing after do, somewhere in London

blocks.note: to act is to do
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Continuing from 10 across: a band performing after a party somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the playing word behind the doing word. Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb in the west of the capital, so a particular location there.

clue.text: Ignore summons — it concerns a writer

blocks.note: to blank someone is to ignore them
to page is to summon someone

explanation.surface: Advice to disregard a call to appear, since it is only about an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerns' is meant in the sense of worries: an empty sheet troubles a writer facing writer's block.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty sheet with nothing written on it is a classic source of worry for authors.

clue.text: Grip doctor learnt hanging around hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered
hanging around means surrounding, so one part wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A medic picked something up while loitering in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like DR or MO, but here it is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip an audience is to hold its attention completely, which is what enthral means.

clue.text: Meet rough ground  in a stiff location

indicators.note: ground as in milled or crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet on uneven terrain somewhere awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough ground' reads as a phrase, but 'rough' is part of the letters and 'ground' is the signal. A stiff is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is where corpses, slangily called stiffs, are kept before burial.

clue.text: Variety of music filter

blocks.note: first meaning: a passage or tune
second meaning: to pass liquid through a sieve

explanation.surface: A type of music used as a sound filter.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun can mean a melody or musical passage, and the verb means to sieve liquid from solids.

clue.text: Gone over again? About time for it to be withdrawn

indicators.note: about means around, so the first part goes round the second

blocks.note: to retrace a path is to go over it again
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Revisiting something, then deciding it is time to take it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that is retracted has been taken back or withdrawn by its maker.

clue.text: Emotional type put out to get feedback

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who feels things strongly
second meaning: a tentative suggestion made to test reactions

explanation.surface: A sensitive person who is upset at being asked for comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests being offended, but it means sent out, as in putting out feelers.
explanation.definitionFit: One who feels is a feeler, and a feeler is also a cautious approach made to sound out opinion.

clue.text: Come again to pick up Brazilian dog

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are taken by ear

blocks.note: a cur from Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: Returning to collect a dog from Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: A cur is a mongrel dog, and Rio stands for Brazil via its famous city.
explanation.definitionFit: To reoccur is to happen once more, which is what come again means of an event.

clue.text: Mark Antony goes first? Just the opposite

blocks.note: taken as written; 'goes first' puts it ahead
M is the abbreviation for mark

explanation.surface: Mark Antony taking the lead, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark Antony' reads as the Roman general, but the two words split, with Antony placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word with the contrary meaning to another, so it is literally the opposite.

clue.text: Worker infected by animal disease while away

indicators.note: infected by means having something get inside, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: a worker ant
BSE is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: An employee catching a livestock illness while off on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, so they are away from the place in question.

clue.text: They are put on to thwart those who tease

definitions.text: They are put on to thwart

blocks.clueFragment: They are put on to thwart
blocks.note: first meaning: from the British idiom 'put the ... on', meaning to spoil or jinx
second meaning: people who ridicule others

explanation.walkthrough: To put the mockers on something is a British expression for ruining its chances.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockers are people who jeer, and in the idiom they are a jinx placed on someone's plans.

clue.text: Workshop central to cloistered feudal priory

indicators.note: central to means at the heart of, so only the middle of each word is used

blocks.note: the two middle letters of a ten-letter word
the two middle letters of a six-letter word
the two middle letters of a six-letter word

explanation.surface: A craft room at the heart of a secluded medieval monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsman's working room, the same as a workshop.

clue.text: Choice of seating providing space to fall into

definitions.text: Choice of seating providing space to fall into

blocks.note: surface reading: a pair of chairs to pick between
setter's reading: the idiom about failing by falling between two options

explanation.walkthrough: To fall between two stools is to fail by being unable to choose between two alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the gap between a pair of seats, where an indecisive person ends up on the floor.

clue.text: Down and out march  …

blocks.note: first meaning: a homeless vagrant
second meaning: to walk heavily for a long way

explanation.surface: A destitute person on a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a homeless wanderer; as a verb it means to trudge or hike a long distance.

clue.text: Panicky father missing trick

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so letters are taken away

blocks.note: frantic means wildly panicked
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A nervous dad who failed to catch a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd prank, a caper or stunt.

clue.text: …  banned initially to avoid being openly offensive

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Continuing from 23 down: something forbidden in the first place to prevent open offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by social custom, so it is forbidden or banned.

clue.text: Conviction is a bitch when it's taken apart

definitions.text: a bitch when it's taken apart

blocks.note: first meaning: a firmly held belief

blocks.clueFragment: a bitch when it's taken apart
blocks.note: second meaning: split into two words, it describes a female dog that is a mother

explanation.surface: Being found guilty is a nightmare once the case is dismantled.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DOG MA: a canine mum, which is what a bitch is.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of firmly held principles, so a belief held with conviction.

clue.text: Policeman deceives bench

blocks.note: to con is to deceive
a bench can be a work table, as in a workbench

explanation.surface: An officer misleading the magistrates in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bench' suggests the magistrates in court, but it is a work surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: Clear role with no time for being above target

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to clear a fence is to go over it
a role is a part in a play
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor getting a part without enough time to rehearse.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, par is the target score for a hole; over par means taking more strokes than that.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf score over par exceeds the expected standard number of strokes, which is the target.

clue.text: Horrific overdraft added to personal debts

blocks.note: OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft
IOUs are informal notes of what one person owes another

explanation.surface: A bank overdraft piled on top of private loans is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repulsive, close in sense to horrible or horrific.
